_schema.certificationId: string  | FK → certification.id (slug). Must match the cert folder name.
_schema.setNumber: integer | Set index. 1 = first set, 2 = second, etc. Must match the filename suffix.

questions.id: string  | SLUG — convention: 'q-<cert-abbrev>-s<N>-<NNN>'. e.g. 'q-mycert-s1-001'. Unique per cert.
questions.topicId: string  | FK → topics.id (slug). Must exist in topics.json. REQUIRED.
questions.subTopicId: string  | FK → subtopics.id (slug). Must exist in subtopics.json and belong to the referenced topicId. REQUIRED.
questions.unitId: string  | FK → units.id (slug). Must exist in units.json and belong to the referenced subTopicId. REQUIRED.
questions.questionText: string  | The full question stem. No trailing whitespace.
questions.questionType: string  | 'single' = one correct answer | 'multiple' = two or more correct answers.
questions.options: array<string> | Min 4 entries. All options must be plausible — no obviously wrong distractors.
questions.correctAnswers: array<string> | Subset of options. Length = 1 for 'single', >= 2 for 'multiple'.
questions.explanation: string  | Min ~20 words. Explain WHY the correct answer is right and why distractors are wrong.
questions.distractorExplanations: object | OPTIONAL. Map of incorrect option text to explanation of why it's wrong. Enhances learning.
questions.difficulty: string  | 'Easy' | 'Medium' | 'Hard'. Target distribution: ~30% Easy, ~45% Medium, ~25% Hard.
questions.tags: array<string> | Min 1 tag. Use service names or concepts. e.g. ['iam', 'least-privilege']

questions.questionText: Which of the following best describes the shared responsibility model in cloud computing?
options: The cloud provider is responsible for all security aspects including customer data
The customer is responsible for all security aspects including physical infrastructure
Security responsibilities are divided between the cloud provider and the customer based on the service model
Security responsibilities are entirely determined by the customer's SLA agreement
correctAnswers: Security responsibilities are divided between the cloud provider and the customer based on the service model
questions.explanation: The shared responsibility model divides security obligations between the cloud provider and the customer. The provider secures the underlying infrastructure (hardware, networking, physical facilities), while the customer is responsible for securing their data, applications, identity management, and configurations. The exact boundary shifts depending on whether the service is IaaS, PaaS, or SaaS.

distractorExplanations.The cloud provider is responsible for al: Incorrect. While the provider secures the infrastructure, customers are always responsible for their own data, access controls, and application security.
distractorExplanations.The customer is responsible for all secu: Incorrect. The cloud provider manages physical security, hardware maintenance, and network infrastructure. Customers don't have access to or responsibility for these layers.
distractorExplanations.Security responsibilities are entirely d: Incorrect. The shared responsibility model is a fundamental cloud security principle that applies regardless of SLA terms. SLAs define service levels, not security boundaries.

questions.questionText: A company wants to reduce cloud costs for a batch processing workload that can tolerate interruptions. Which pricing model is most appropriate?
options: On-demand instances at full price
Reserved instances with a 3-year commitment
Spot/Preemptible instances
Dedicated hosts with per-socket licensing
questions.explanation: Spot (AWS) or Preemptible (GCP) instances use spare cloud capacity at discounts of up to 90%. They can be reclaimed by the provider with short notice, making them ideal for fault-tolerant, interruptible batch workloads. On-demand is full price, reserved requires upfront commitment, and dedicated hosts are the most expensive option.

questions.questionText: Your application requires automatic scaling based on CPU utilization and must support zero-downtime deployments. Which compute approach best satisfies both requirements?
options: A single large VM with manual scaling
A managed instance group with autoscaling and rolling update policy
A serverless function with a fixed concurrency limit
A container deployed on a single node without orchestration
correctAnswers: A managed instance group with autoscaling and rolling update policy
questions.explanation: Managed instance groups (MIGs) support CPU-based autoscaling policies that add or remove instances automatically. Rolling update policies replace instances incrementally, ensuring zero downtime. A single VM cannot scale, serverless functions have concurrency limits not tied to CPU, and unorchestrated containers lack both features.

questions.questionText: Which two storage characteristics should guide your choice between object storage and a relational database? (Choose 2)
options: Object storage is optimized for structured, queryable data with ACID transactions
Object storage is ideal for large unstructured files like images and backups
Relational databases provide ACID transactions and support complex SQL queries
Relational databases are the lowest-cost option for storing large binary files
Object storage supports row-level locking for concurrent write operations
correctAnswers: Object storage is ideal for large unstructured files like images and backups
Relational databases provide ACID transactions and support complex SQL queries
questions.explanation: Object storage (e.g. Cloud Storage, S3) is designed for large, unstructured blobs — images, videos, backups — with high durability and low cost per GB. Relational databases (e.g. Cloud SQL, RDS) provide ACID transactions, foreign keys, and SQL query support for structured data. Object storage does not support SQL queries or row-level locking, and relational databases are expensive for large binary files.

questions.questionText: A team wants to define their cloud infrastructure as code to enable repeatable, version-controlled deployments. Which approach is most aligned with this goal?
options: Manually configure resources through the cloud console and document the steps
Use Infrastructure as Code (IaC) tools such as Terraform or Deployment Manager
Write shell scripts that call the CLI and store them in a shared folder
Use the cloud provider's GUI wizard and export the configuration as a PDF
correctAnswers: Use Infrastructure as Code (IaC) tools such as Terraform or Deployment Manager
questions.explanation: Infrastructure as Code (IaC) tools like Terraform, Pulumi, or cloud-native tools (Deployment Manager, CloudFormation) define infrastructure in declarative configuration files that can be version-controlled, reviewed, and applied consistently. Manual console steps are error-prone and not reproducible. Shell scripts lack state management and drift detection. PDF exports are not executable.

questions.questionText: You need to allow traffic from the internet to reach a web server in a private subnet while preventing direct internet access to the server's private IP. Which component achieves this?
options: A VPN gateway with site-to-site connectivity
A NAT gateway for outbound traffic only
A load balancer with a public IP in a public subnet forwarding to the private instance
A direct peering connection between the VPC and the internet
correctAnswers: A load balancer with a public IP in a public subnet forwarding to the private instance
questions.explanation: A load balancer sits in a public subnet with a public IP, accepting inbound internet traffic and forwarding it to backend instances in private subnets. The private instances never expose their IPs directly to the internet. A VPN gateway is for private network-to-network connectivity. A NAT gateway only handles outbound traffic from private subnets. Direct peering exposes the VPC directly.

questions.questionText: Your team needs to be alerted when error rate on a production API exceeds 5% over a 5-minute window. What is the correct sequence of steps?
options: Create a log sink → export to BigQuery → run a scheduled query → send email
Create a log-based metric for error responses → create an alerting policy with a threshold condition → configure a notification channel
Enable audit logging → create a dashboard → manually check every 5 minutes
Deploy a sidecar container that polls the API and sends alerts via webhook
correctAnswers: Create a log-based metric for error responses → create an alerting policy with a threshold condition → configure a notification channel
questions.explanation: The standard observability pattern is: (1) create a log-based metric that counts error-status responses, (2) create an alerting policy that fires when the metric exceeds the threshold over the evaluation window, (3) attach a notification channel (email, PagerDuty, Slack). Log sinks to BigQuery add latency. Manual checks are not automated. Sidecar pollers are fragile and non-standard.

questions.questionText: Following the principle of least privilege, which approach is correct when granting a service account access to read objects from a single Cloud Storage bucket?
options: Grant the service account the Owner role at the project level
Grant the service account the Storage Object Viewer role at the bucket level
Grant the service account the Editor role at the project level
Grant the service account the Storage Admin role at the project level
correctAnswers: Grant the service account the Storage Object Viewer role at the bucket level
questions.explanation: Least privilege means granting only the permissions needed for the task, at the narrowest scope. Storage Object Viewer grants read-only access to objects — exactly what is needed. Granting it at the bucket level (not project level) further restricts the scope to that single bucket. Owner, Editor, and Storage Admin all grant far more permissions than required and at a broader scope.

questions.questionText: A startup needs to run a containerized API that scales to zero when idle and only incurs cost during active request processing. Which service model is most appropriate?
options: A dedicated VM running the container 24/7
A Kubernetes cluster with a minimum node count of 1
A fully managed serverless container platform that scales to zero
A bare-metal server with Docker installed
correctAnswers: A fully managed serverless container platform that scales to zero
questions.explanation: Serverless container platforms (e.g. Cloud Run, AWS App Runner) scale to zero when there are no requests, eliminating idle costs. They charge only for CPU and memory consumed during request processing. A dedicated VM or bare-metal server incurs cost 24/7. A Kubernetes cluster with a minimum node count of 1 still has baseline infrastructure costs even when idle.

questions.questionText: Which two features are required to enable private connectivity between two VPCs in the same cloud provider without routing traffic over the public internet? (Choose 2)
options: VPC Peering between the two VPCs
A public IP address on each VPC's gateway
Non-overlapping CIDR ranges on both VPCs
An internet gateway attached to both VPCs
A Cloud CDN distribution in front of each VPC
correctAnswers: VPC Peering between the two VPCs
Non-overlapping CIDR ranges on both VPCs
questions.explanation: VPC Peering establishes a private network route between two VPCs, keeping traffic off the public internet. A prerequisite is that the two VPCs must have non-overlapping CIDR ranges — overlapping ranges make routing ambiguous and peering will fail. Public IPs, internet gateways, and CDN distributions are not required and would route traffic publicly.
